notes:
- Battery saver can be told to leave the checks alone: AniList has no push stream, so a new event is found by a periodic check - and Android may defer that check for battery saving, sometimes for hours on a phone that has been off the charger. Notification settings now has a Battery optimisation card: it reports whether Android exempts the app and opens the system dialog that grants the exemption, with Android's own exemption list and the app's details page as fallbacks for the phones that do not answer the direct request. The card also says what the exemption does not promise: a check still needs a connection, and a manufacturer's own battery manager can ignore the platform list.
- The alert you tapped shows you the post: Tapping an activity alert already opened the Activity tab scrolled to the post it named, but on a feed of near-identical cards nothing said which row was the destination, so the arrival read as "the app opened somewhere in the list". That row now draws a ring that arrives at full strength and fades out over about two seconds: two strokes of the card's own outline, drawn over the card in the draw phase rather than blurred, so a long feed does not pay for a render pass per row.
- The trailer plays again: The wrapper page identified itself as https://www.youtube.com, and YouTube reads that as YouTube embedding itself: every trailer came back as error 152 - 'This video is unavailable' - before a frame played. The page now loads under the app's own https origin, which is the Referer YouTube now requires (a missing one is error 153), and the player is told that same origin for its API and its attribution. The iframe still comes from youtube-nocookie.com; the page's identity and the player's host were never supposed to be the same value.
- Watch on YouTube leaves the app: The one link YouTube offers on a refused video - and any other link a reader taps - stayed inside the player and replaced the trailer with the watch page in a 16:9 hole with no back button. That button is a new-window link and this player has no popup window, so it arrives in the player's own frame; the rule now keeps only the player's own pages - the embed, its error card, its consent screen - and sends the watch page out through the shared opener. If nothing can take the address it is copied instead of the tap doing nothing.
- The trailer works sideways: Two things broke the moment the phone was turned. The frame was 16:9 at the window's width, which on a phone on its side is 450dp of picture on a 360dp screen, so the close button, the bottom of the video and the way out to YouTube were off the display; it is offered the room the chrome leaves and fits inside it, and portrait keeps exactly the geometry it had. And the flag that opened the player was plain remember, so the rotation rebuilt the tree and closed it - the one moment a reader asks for landscape was the moment the player went away. The flag is saved now, so the player reopens on its side; the embed reloads from the start, because a WebView belongs to the activity that created it and cannot outlive a recreation.
- A trailer with no id still leaves a link: The external hand-off for a trailer AniList did not give an id for used a raw intent whose failure was swallowed, so a device with no browser got no browser, no message and no URL. It uses the app's shared opener now, which copies the address when it cannot open it.
- The poster flies home again: The copy was taken out of the composition at the landing in v2.6.8 to stop a second poster living for the whole session, but the close then re-staged one that no longer existed: the page hid its poster, the sheet dismissed and nothing flew back to the card. It stays composed at alpha zero now - the flight asks Coil for the card rectangle, so the picture it holds is the card's cache entry rather than a second decode - and the close starts on the frame it does.
- The poster's frame travels too: The flying copy drew the art, the tint and the shadow but not the hairline the page draws around the poster, so the frame appeared a frame after the landing - one edge left out of a hand-off that exists to hide exactly that. Both heroes now hand their stroke to the flight and the copy carries it for the whole way, scaled with the picture rather than sitting at a fixed width while it is still small.
- The flight leaves from the picture the card already has: The copy asked Coil for the poster at its original size, which is a different cache key from the card that was on screen a frame earlier: a fresh, full-resolution decode that often outlived the six-frame wait, so the open gave up and cut to the page. It asks for the card rectangle now - the entry the card just filled - and growing that picture is the flight. That is why the animation used to run only sometimes.
- A poster that is loading says what it is: Both title pages drew a flat cover colour until the poster decoded, which reads as a missing picture, and kept it if the request never resolved. They draw the same initials tile the cards have drawn since the grid first had a cold start, with the artwork dissolving over it.
- A tier label is readable on its own colour: The gutter label on every row was white, and white on the palette's amber is 1.6:1 - not a faint label but an unreadable one, and the small count beneath it was worse. The label and the count now take black or white by whichever has the higher contrast against the row's own fill, so amber, gold and grey go black while brown and violet stay white; every colour the palette offers now clears the WCAG small-text floor of 4.5:1 instead of ten of the twelve failing it. The count under the label also lost the 82% alpha it was drawn at: fading the chosen ink put violet and indigo back under the floor, so the count is quieter by being smaller, not by being fainter. The board, the SVG export and the PNG export all ask one shared function, so a board exported to a file cannot disagree with the screen it was exported from.
- The tier list shows its colours before it is opened: A list in the tier library showed its name and how many titles it held and nothing about the tiers inside it, so two lists looked identical until one of them was opened. Each row now leads with a small stack of bars in the list's own tier colours - up to five, in the board's order - and the 'Carry on with' card does the same. Each stack is one canvas: no image is decoded and no five composables are laid out to draw five rectangles.
- A press that becomes a scroll lets go: Eleven controls that draw their own press spring - the palette cards and hue chips under Appearance, the canvas chip, the title page's hero chips, a cast card, a sequel's parent card, a title row's copy button, a notification row, a tier search poster, a saved joke's action and a voiced-character card on a person's page - each installed a second pointer loop beside the tap they already had. A finger that started a scroll on one of them sprang it down and back up again, two gestures from one, and every row of every scrolling list paid for an extra pointer-input coroutine. They share the tap's own interaction source now, so the press ends the moment the gesture is claimed as a drag. The controls with no press state to share, a bare Button among them, keep the loop and their feedback.
- A closed trailer stops holding its player: Closing the trailer destroyed its WebView but left the seven-second safety timer queued: the reveal could still fire against a view the composition had already thrown away, and the page - with the audio decoder behind it - stayed alive until the timer ran out. The timer is cancelled when the player's view detaches, which is the one hook that fires both for a close and for the rotation that recreates the dialog.
- A pinch no longer rebuilds the page around the board: The board's zoom was a value read by the screen's own body, so the toolbar readout, the sheet host and the persistence effect all subscribed to it: every frame of a pinch recomposed the whole page - the tray, both toolbars and every sheet slot - only to pass the board a number it already had. The zoom now lives in a small saved holder that the board and the stepper read and the page merely carries. The board's measurement pass stopped building a list of row, poster and caret objects on each frame as well: it walks the same children in order twice, once to measure and once to place.
